full_judgment: 3. The case of the pre-emptor in short is this that the property of the case land along with remaining property of the plot originally belonged to Syed Moulovi Siddique and Syed Abdur Rahman both are sons of Syed Sheanatullah and others which was correctly recorded in Revisional Khatian No.416T. The said RS recorded owner Abdur Rahman died leaving behind his one son named Abdul Hye and two daughters Masuda Khatun and Mostafa Khatun. Mostafa Khatun died leaving behind her four sons including pre-emptor and her husband Syed Rezaul Amin. Abdul Hye died leaving behind his three sons co-sharer respondent Nos. 19-21. The said RS recorded owner Syed Moulovi Siddique died leaving behind his three sons Ahmed Hossain, Abul Hossain and Abdul Quader. Abul Hossain died without any wife son or daughter. Abdul Quader died leaving behind one son and one daughter co-sharer, respondent Nos.11 and 12. Moulovi Ahmed Hossain died leaving behind his four sons one daughter and one wife seller respondent Nos.5-10. The names of above mentioned successor-in-interest of said RS recorded owner Moulovi Siddique and Moulovi Abdur Rahman were duly recorded in BS Khatian No.824. The suit property in RS Plot No. 9605 corresponds to BS Plot No.12081. Out of 15 decimal land in the said BS Plot No. 12081 the successors-in-interest of Moulovi Syed Siddique became the owner of 7 and 1/2, decimals land in 8 annas share and successor-in-interest of Moulovi Syed Abdur Rahman became the owner of remaining 7 and 1/2 decimals land in remaining 8 annas share. Thereafter the successors-in-interest of Moulovi Abdur Rahman entered into a Mutual Agreement through a registered deed of Awaz (ie Deed of Exchange) being deed No.124 duly registered on 7-1-1982 in the Sub-Registrar's Office, Rangunia, Chittagong for the useful and convenient enjoyment of their property. Thus the pre-emptor-appellant and his other three brothers (ie co-sharers-respondent Nos.13- 15) along with their father became the owner of 7 and 1/2 decimals of land in the western part of the said BS Plot No.12081 by virtue of inheritance and deed of awaj. They have been enjoying the said land as a homestead since 1982 by constructing house and growing trees. The remaining 7 and 1/2 decimal of land situated at the eastern part of the said plot No.BS 12081 was owned and enjoyed by the successors-in-interest of said Moulovi Siddique (ie present seller-respondent Nos. 5-10). The preemptees along with their father, respondent No. 1 (presently an associate of pre-emptor-appellant) are living together in a joint family and also a stranger purchaser to the suit land.
